Selected photographers pay a print and installation fee, from €45 for prints up to 40cm on the longest side, or may ship their own exhibit-ready prints; work need not be for sale, and the gallery commission on any sale is 25%. — Deadline: November 9, 2026. Fee: €25–€50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 20th Biennial Joyce Elaine Grant Photography Exhibition · Texas Woman's University
item.description: The twentieth edition of the biennial Joyce Elaine Grant Photography Exhibition, a national juried show at Texas Woman's University's East | West Galleries in Denton, running February 15 – March 12, 2027. Established in 2001 by TWU and the Photographic Artists' Coalition, a student-run photography organisation, JEG was founded by alumna Christine Shank and a small group of graduate students and named in memory of the mother of Professor Susan kae Grant, Cornaro Professor of Visual Art Emerita. Every edition is juried by a distinguished female curator; this one is judged by Maria L. Kelly, Assistant Curator of Photography at the High Museum of Art in Atlanta, who has helped organise nearly thirty photography installations there — among them Photography's New Vision: Experiments in Seeing (2025), Tyler Mitchell: Idyllic Space (2024), Underexposed: Women Photographers from the Collection (2021) and Helen Levitt: In the Street (2015) — and has curated at Friche la Belle de Mai in Marseille, Emory University, Swan Coach House Gallery and Columbus State University. Beyond selecting the group show, the juror awards one artist a solo exhibition in the TWU East | West Galleries, scheduled during the following JEG Exhibition. Open-themed and open to photographers, lens-based or lensless, video and photo-related artists based in the United States; all photographic and related processes are encouraged, including digital, video, non-silver, photo and mixed media, and photographic book arts. Work must not exceed 60 inches in any dimension. Judging is online from JPEGs of at least 1200 pixels on the longest side and no more than 5 MB; one to five images cost $35 (Basic Application) and up to ten cost $60 (Expanded Application), with fees non-refundable and treated as donations to the JEG Endowment, which funds photography scholarships for TWU graduate students. Accepted artists are notified by December 9, 2026, pay their own shipping both ways, and must deliver ready-to-hang work (D-rings and wire, Plexiglas not glass) to the gallery by February 5, 2027. The organiser's own entry page gives the deadline as November 9 while its CaFÉ listing states entries close at midnight Central on November 8 — the earlier of the two is stored here. That entry page also still prints a link to the retired 2024 CaFÉ listing, which now loads an empty page; the live listing is the one linked here. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–5 images), $60 (up to 10 images). Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: BLUE Photography Exhibit · Decode Gallery
item.description: Decode Gallery's juried exhibition on the colour blue, in every hue and shade — landscapes and seascapes, portraits and abstracts, and whatever the gallery calls the calm or melancholy the colour stirs up. The call is open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional alike, and there is no restriction on genre or process. At least 26 images are selected by juror Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer who founded Decode after a BA in Photography from the Art Institute of Seattle. Selected photographers pay nothing further: the gallery handles all printing itself on an Epson printer with Ilford Pearl paper and presents work in museum-quality 22 x 22 inch white frames with precut white mats (11 x 11, 10 x 15, 11 x 15, 12 x 15 inches and others), scaling files for the best fit in the mat without ever cropping them. One exhibition print is made per image and archived in a flat file for six months after the show. Entry is $40 for up to five photographs or $45 for up to ten. Photographers are notified by email within two weeks of the deadline, and high-resolution files are due two days after the acceptance email. The exhibition runs January 2 to January 30 at the gallery in Tucson, opening January 2. Work may optionally be listed for sale, with Decode taking a 50 per cent commission; all rights to the image file and the print remain with the photographer. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $45/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: SQUARE Photography Exhibit 2027 · Decode Gallery
item.description: The next edition of Decode Gallery's square-format show, challenging photographers to compose within the confines of the perfect square — from analog Hasselblads to digital Instagram feeds, the most persistent format in photography, where symmetry, balance, focus and narrative are all transformed by equal sides. Submissions are welcome from every photographic genre, including portraiture, landscape, documentary, architecture and conceptual work; the call is open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional alike. Twelve images are selected by juror Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer who founded Decode after a BA in Photography from the Art Institute of Seattle, and hang for an unusually long three months — February 6 to April 24, 2027 — at the gallery in Tucson, opening February 6. Selected photographers pay nothing further: the gallery handles all printing itself on an Epson printer with Ilford Pearl paper and presents work in museum-quality 14 x 14 inch frames with mats cut to 7 x 7 inches. One print is made per accepted image file and archived in a flat file for six months after the show. Entry is a flat $40 per entry, which the gallery's guidelines describe as covering up to ten photographs; the live entry form itself accepts fifteen files before it refuses more, so the ten is the entitlement the gallery states rather than a limit the form imposes. Photographers are notified by email within two weeks of the deadline. Work may optionally be listed for sale, with Decode taking a 50 per cent commission; all rights to the image file and the print remain with the photographer. The gallery states plainly that a paid entry does not guarantee a place in any exhibition. — Deadline: January 7, 2027. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: As Above, So Below — SaveArtSpace Bus Shelter Exhibition
item.description: Public art exhibition on bus shelter advertising space in Miami during Miami Art Week, curated by the illustrator and muralist Marlon Pruz and opening November 27, 2026. As Above, So Below explores the idea that the patterns of the universe are reflected within us and that the inner world is inseparable from the outer one, considering the relationship between the cosmic and the earthly, the microscopic and the infinite — the way electrons orbiting an atomic nucleus mimic planets orbiting the sun, and the way the golden ratio and other recurring patterns in nature suggest an underlying order connecting all forms of life. Pruz says he is looking for work that creates a strong visual or conceptual dialogue between these realms: imagery connecting the body to nature, humanity to the cosmos, consciousness to environment, and the intimate to the infinite. The entry form gives the theme more plainly as Visionary Art and states that all art will be accepted. Open to artists of any age, skill level or background; corporate logos, personal advertising and video are excluded and still JPEGs only are accepted, so photographic work is eligible. Up to ten images may be uploaded at a maximum of 2 MB each, with high-resolution files requested from selected artists; the potential ad panel is 69 inches high by 48 inches wide, though the artwork itself can be any size. Submissions run September 23 to October 19, 2026 at 11:59pm, selected artists are announced after November 2, and the work goes up on Miami ad space from November 27 for at least one month. SaveArtSpace is a 501(c)(3) non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial ad space since 2015; fees are tax-deductible donations that pay for the ad space, and every exhibition is curated, so applying does not guarantee installation. The entry form charges the stated donation plus card fees, so the amount actually taken at checkout is $36.92 for one to three images, rising to $108.45 for ten. — Deadline: October 19, 2026. Fee: $35 (1–3 images), $10 each additional. Prize: Bus shelter exhibition in Miami.

item.title: Empty Places : Abandoned Spaces · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: International juried photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on emptiness, absence and abandonment. The gallery's framing distinguishes the two: an empty place is not necessarily abandoned, and an abandoned space is rarely without evidence — one is defined by absence, the other by what remains, and both invite the same questions: who was here, what happened, why does the place continue to hold our attention. Praxis is looking for work on the visual and emotional weight of emptiness, from derelict factories and rural ruins to neglected homes, civic structures, vacant interiors and landscapes emptied of human presence, whether it documents decay or transforms emptiness into something poetic, symbolic, uncanny or surreal; the entry portal adds that all lens-based art is welcome. Up to 74 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (21 November – 12 December 2026), featured on the gallery's online exhibition page and permanently archived there. Awards are a Juror's Choice (free entry into three future juried calls of the artist's choice), a Directors' Choice (two future calls) and eight honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, the printed exhibition catalogue and the online gallery — there is no cash prize. Entrants must be 18 or older, and images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's optional $37 printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing in its 22 × 22-inch black frames (mat openings up to 11 × 11, 10 × 15, 11.8 × 15 or 8 × 15 inches) and retains a 50% commission on any print sales. Notification is 30 October 2026. No juror is named for this call on either the gallery's own page or the entry portal, unlike its sibling call on the same page. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Roadside Attractions: Art and History on Route 66
item.description: Gallery Seven and the Gaylord Building Historic Site are mounting this juried show together for Route 66's centennial, pairing an art component curated by the gallery with a history component built by the Gaylord Building, and it runs long — 12 November 2026 to 24 March 2027 in the Third Floor Founders' Gallery of the Gaylord Building in Lockport, Illinois, a National Trust site on the old highway itself. The brief is the legacy of Route 66 in Illinois and beyond, read both as a real transportation corridor and as a symbol of travel, community, roadside culture and American imagination. Photography is in: the prospectus states that all media is eligible except film/video, oversized works and special installations, and Gallery Seven has run Open Lens, its own community photography exhibition, every year since 2010. Open to any artist 18 or over with no geographic bar — the gallery accepts shipped work as well as drop-off, and will advise on shipping on request. One $50 fee covers up to five entries, with an extra image allowed free for each 3D piece. Awards total $800 in cash: Best of Show $250, 1st $175, 2nd $125, 3rd $100 and three Honorable Mentions of $50, presented at a 6–7pm ceremony on 10 March 2027; the gallery's own web page also names a People's Choice Award voted by visitors. Work must be original, never previously submitted to or shown at Gallery Seven, framed with hanging wire and bumpers, and no taller than 48 inches or wider than 36 including the frame. Everything must be for sale at the artist's own price with a 30% commission to the gallery, paid out within 45 days of closing; sold work stays on the wall to the end. Entries go by email as .jpg attachments at 72 DPI and 3000 pixels on the long side, with the entry form, and the fee is paid by PayPal on the gallery's site, by cheque or in person — note the two closing dates: email entries are accepted to 24 October 2026, but if you post a CD with the form instead it must be postmarked by 17 October. Selections are notified 28–29 October and delivered 5–7 November. The prospectus says entries are juried by independent jurors to be announced, while the gallery's own web page says the show will be juried and judged by the artist partners of Gallery Seven; no name is published either way. Anything left at the gallery after 24 March 2027 becomes its property. — Deadline: October 24, 2026. Fee: $50 for up to 5 works. Prize: $250 Best of Show + $175 1st + $125 2nd + $100 3rd + 3 × $50 Honorable Mention.

item.title: 2027 REAF Regional Erotic Art Show and Sale · Rochester Erotic Arts Festival
item.description: The juried art show at the heart of the Rochester Erotic Arts Festival, an adults-only weekend of art, performance, workshops and vending that moves to Ithaca for 2027 after losing its Auburn hotel. REAF is looking for high-quality original work that is "creative, erotic and thought-provoking", and photography is not a tolerated extra here — it is named in the accepted-media list alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, mixed media, collage, digital art, film and sculpture, and it has its own top award: Best in Photography, $100, matched by Best in Fine Art at $100 and three Producers Choice Awards of $50. Accepted artists get a free weekend Artist Pass to the whole festival and can buy a plus-one pass for $30. Work is offered for sale and REAF takes no commission — artists supply their own buyer contact details, which are displayed with the work, and deal with buyers directly. One entry is $30 and covers up to five pieces; an artist may file up to three entries, so fifteen pieces is the practical ceiling at $90. Work must not have been shown at REAF before. THIS IS A HAND-DELIVERY SHOW AND THAT IS THE REAL GATE: accepted work has to be brought in person to Ithaca, New York on the evening of Thursday 8 April or the morning of Friday 9 April 2027, ready to hang — matted, framed, signed and labelled — and cannot be collected before the exhibition closes; there is no shipping option, and the organiser describes the show as regional without naming a region. Prints other than photographs must be limited editions on archival paper, numbered and signed. Artists must be 18 or over, must hold a model release for any identifiable person photographed, and where a model is nude or in sexual activity must hold a legible copy of ID proving they were 18+; work depicting minors is refused outright. REAF carries no insurance on displayed work and recommends artists check their own. Submissions are open now; the deadline is 1 February 2027, decisions go out by 8 February, and accepted artists must respond by 15 February. The festival itself runs 9–11 April 2027 across the Ithaca Downtown Conference Center and The Hotel Ithaca, with ASL interpreters available all weekend. — Deadline: February 1, 2027. Fee: $30 per entry of up to 5 works. Prize: $100 Best in Photography + $100 Best in Fine Art + 3 × $50 Producers Choice.

item.title: 27th Annual Joan L. Dunfey Open Juried Exhibition · New Hampshire Art Association
item.description: NHAA's long-running open-themed juried show at the Robert Lincoln Levy Gallery in Portsmouth, now in its 27th year, honouring Joan L. Dunfey (1925–1998), a Seacoast patron of the arts whose fund still supports artists. It is open to artists across New England working in all mediums, and the association's programme makes clear photography counts — it also runs the annual Lotte Jacobi Juried Show in the same gallery. There is no set subject: the jury is looking for strong work of any kind. Sarah Elliott, Lecturer of Painting and Drawing at the University of New Hampshire, is the juror; she trained at Boston University and worked for years in Germany, Hong Kong, Italy, China and France, and her own practice moves between figurative and non-figurative oil, watercolour and charcoal. Artists may submit one to three works, original, completed in the last three years and not previously shown at the gallery. 2D framed work is capped at 60 inches in the longest dimension including frame; freestanding 3D work at 42 inches in any dimension; wall-hung 3D over 35 pounds needs the artist's help to install. Every entry needs an image of at least 1200px on the long side plus title, medium, dimensions, year and retail price, and a short artist statement. All work must be for sale at $100 or more, with a 60/40 split in the artist's favour, and artists arrange their own delivery, pickup and transit insurance. Prizes go to first, second and third place plus an Artist Under 30 Award, and entry is free for anyone under 30 thanks to an anonymous donor. Non-members pay $40 to $50 depending on how many works they enter, members $20 to $30. The exhibition runs 4–29 November 2026, with acceptances out by 5pm on Friday 16 October, drop-off 1–2 November and an opening reception on 6 November, 5–8pm. — Deadline: October 7, 2026. Fee: $40–$50 (NHAA members $20–$30; free for artists under 30). Prize: Exhibition + awards.

item.title: 30×30 Call Out — Annual Exhibition 2027 · Visual Arts Scotland
item.description: Visual Arts Scotland invites its members to submit small-format work for the popular 30×30 display within its 2027 Annual Exhibition in the Upper Galleries of the Royal Scottish Academy Building, Edinburgh; the exhibition runs January 8 to February 3, 2027. The 30×30 is the show's affordable section: work is offered for sale from shelves and in print racks, priced at £250 or under, with VAS taking 40% commission on sales (35% for Professional Members). Maximum two works per artist, each presented on a precisely 30×30 cm mount — the artwork itself may be smaller — made within the last two years, wrapped in clear cellophane and labelled on the back with artist name, title, medium and price. Work on paper should be on good-quality backing card; card mounts must be of professional quality; maximum thickness of the wrapped work is 2–3 mm, with no canvases on stretchers accepted. Work previously shown with VAS or at the RSA should not be submitted, and artists insure their own work. Register each piece through the linked Google Form, whose stated closing date for submissions is 27 November 2026, then post work to the VAS studio at Out of the Blue Drill Hall, Edinburgh to arrive by Friday 18 December 2026 (the form gives 22 December), or hand-deliver to the RSA upper galleries on Sunday 3 January 2027. No entry fee, and no jury: VAS lists "Guaranteed inclusion in the members 30X30 section of the Annual Exhibition" among its membership benefits, though the form notes VAS may reject work that is poorly presented or does not fit the presentation guidance. Membership is required: £40 a year for General membership, £28 for Emerging (students, recent graduates and artists under 23), with fee support for artists living with disability or receiving universal credit; VAS offers it to "artists and makers engaged in the visual arts and/or contemporary craft in Scotland". Media are not enumerated for the 30×30 itself, but the parent Annual Exhibition welcomes "all areas of visual arts and contemporary crafts, including but not limited to painting, printmaking, fine-art photography, drawing", and the 30×30 rules explicitly accommodate work on paper. — Deadline: November 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + sales.

item.title: Queens Arts Fund: New Work Grant 2027 · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description: A project grant of $3,000 to $7,500 for Queens-based artists to make new work — work that has not been produced or presented to an audience before. The Queens Arts Fund is administered by NYFA and supported by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs through the Greater New York Arts Development Fund, in partnership with the City Council. Photography is a named discipline: applications are sorted to peer-review panels by discipline, and Visual Arts explicitly covers Painting, Photography, Printmaking/Drawing/Book Arts and Craft/Sculpture. To apply you must live in Queens or hold a full-time studio lease there (PO boxes are not accepted), be at least 18 by 31 December 2026, and propose a project with a free or sliding-scale public component — an exhibition, screening, reading or workshop — taking place in Queens between 1 January and 31 December 2027. Artist collectives may apply through one Queens-based lead applicant. Grant funds can cover artist fees (the fund actively encourages applicants to pay themselves), technical assistance, planning and preparation, supplies and materials, venue rental for the project, in-state travel and marketing, with individual supply items capped at $1,000. The equipment line is narrower than it first looks: cameras and lighting are eligible only as equipment “related to the creation and promotion of virtual programming”, and equipment or capital goods whose total exceeds $1,000 are ineligible outright. Studio or living rent, residency fees, acquisitions, out-of-state travel and reception catering cannot be covered. Applications are scored by peer panels on four equally weighted criteria including creativity and artistic merit, and recipients may be awarded 50–100% of what they request, so the form asks for a contingency plan. Only one application to either Queens Arts Fund programme is allowed per applicant per year; non-profit organisations apply instead to the QAF Arts Access Grant. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,000–$7,500.

item.title: X ROID Cologne 2027 · The Stage Gallery
item.description: The Stage Gallery's international instant art expo returns to Cologne, the city where it began as InstantCologne in 2019, after editions in Cologne, Bonn, Vienna and Basel. X ROID Cologne 2027 runs 21–23 May 2027 at the gallery's new Cologne location on Gottesweg, a three-day festival of instant photography with a Pola Walk through the city and an international gathering of instant artists. Only original instant photographs are eligible — no prints. Accepted formats are SX-70, 600, Spectra, Packfilm, Square, Wide and Mini, from Polaroid, Polaroid Originals, Impossible Project and Fuji Instax. One exhibition space holds up to 4 Polaroids (SX-70/600/Packfilm) or a maximum of 2 8x10-inch Polaroids, and artists may book multiple spaces — the fee is charged per space, so a second space doubles it. The participation fee covers professional framing of the work by the gallery (own frames by arrangement) and inclusion in the exhibition catalogue, and — a change from the Bonn edition, which took 25% — the gallery takes no sales commission at all, so artists keep 100% of any sale. Return shipping is not included. The exhibition is juried and curated by The Stage Gallery itself; no outside juror is named, and there is no cash prize. Applying is a binding commitment: the organiser states that acceptance makes the participation fee due and non-refundable even if the artist then cancels. Copyright stays with the artist throughout, with a promotional-use licence for the gallery and the catalogue. Application is by email to submissions@thestagegallery.com with the subject line “Application X roid Cologne 2027”, artist and contact details, and JPG files at 1000px on the longest side. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: €170 per exhibition space (early bird, until Oct 18) / €220 from Oct 19. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Revelations · LoosenArt
item.description: LoosenArt's open call for Issue Collective #3, a publication dedicated to what emerges beneath the surface of things. The call asks what it means to reveal something today, and what appears when we look more closely, listen more carefully and move past the veil of appearances — revelation as a moment of insight, discovery or unveiling, whether an unexpected perspective, a personal truth or an overlooked aspect of reality. Entry is free and open worldwide, and the organiser lists the accepted media plainly: photography, video, digital, visual design, visual data, installation, sculpture and painting. Each artist may submit one to three works. Beyond the publication, a selection of the works chosen for it will be considered in a further selection process leading to a group exhibition to be held in 2027 in one of three Italian cities — Milan, Rome or Cagliari — which the organiser has not yet fixed. Submission is through a Google Form — the same form LoosenArt uses for the Aesthetic Dynamics call running alongside this one, with a required “Select the call of interest” dropdown that assigns your entry to this one. It asks for name, country, email, website, Instagram, an artist statement of up to 70 words in English, and up to three files of no more than 5 MB each, renamed for the work's title. LoosenArt's site is a spare Google Sites presence run from Quartu Sant'Elena in Sardinia, and beyond the call text it publishes no further terms; no charge of any kind is mentioned at any stage. — Deadline: November 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 2027 Black Creativity Juried Art Exhibition — Teen Category · Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
item.description: The teen half of Black Creativity, the longest continually running exhibition of African American art in the United States, shown at Chicago's Griffin Museum of Science and Industry since 1970 and now in its 57th year. The Teen Category is free to enter and open to Black teen artists in the Chicagoland area — within 100 miles of the museum — who are enrolled in grades 9 through 12 in the 2026/27 school year; the General Category runs alongside it for adult artists nationwide. Contemporary work in any visual medium is accepted, and the museum's own exhibition page names photography outright among the media it shows. Submit up to four works made during the last school year or since, anonymously, each original and unsold and not previously selected for a Black Creativity exhibition; a teacher or caregiver may help with the technical side but the artist submits for themselves. The same three jurors judge both categories. Teen awards are $600 for Best in Show, $375 for second place and $250 for third, and selected work hangs in the exhibition from January 18 to April 18, 2027. Accepted work must arrive framed or otherwise finished and ready to install, with delivery and pickup by the artist — 2D work may not exceed 60 inches in any direction, 3D work 30 inches, and nothing may weigh more than 50 pounds. Acceptances go out by November 4, 2026, local drop-off is December 18–19 and work is collected April 23–24, 2027. The museum does not solicit sales, but artists may sell from the walls and no commission is taken. AI-generated work is not accepted. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $600 / $375 / $250 + Exhibition.

item.title: The Eye of Readers — Portfolio Submissions · L'Œil de la Photographie
item.description: Every weekend L'Œil de la Photographie — published in English as The Eye of Photography — gives an issue over to its readers, publishing a selection of portfolios sent in from around the world. The magazine publishes daily in both English and French out of Paris, and the readers' section sits alongside its regular coverage of exhibitions, festivals, books and photographers. The magazine states the section is open to amateurs and professionals alike. Submission is free and rolling: there is no deadline and no entry fee, and selected portfolios are published on the magazine's site with the artist's text and a link to their website. What is asked is a coherent series of 12 to 15 photographs and a text about the series, with a title and, if there is one, a website link; English and French versions of the text are appreciated. Files must be jpg or jpeg, at least 1350 pixels wide for horizontals and 1200 pixels high for verticals, between 150KB and 2MB each, named series-title-lastname-firstname-photonumber.jpg. The magazine is blunt that the specification is a filter in itself: any submission that does not strictly follow these guidelines will not be considered. Entries go through a JotForm the magazine links from its own guidelines page; there is no selection fee, no publication fee and no membership requirement — the paid Premium membership on the same site buys archive access to readers, and is unrelated to submitting. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Delfina Foundation — Brooks International Fellowship 2027
item.description: Two six-month fellowships run jointly by Delfina Foundation and Tate, now in the programme's thirteenth year, placing international researchers inside Tate Britain's Curatorial Division from 5 April to 17 September 2027 while living in residence at Delfina Foundation in London. The two strands are separate calls with separate application forms. The first, Leonora Carrington: Art and the Theatre of Life, asks a Fellow to undertake foundational research into the British-Mexican artist's interest in theatre, performance and performativity — locating, analysing and contextualising theatrical materials across archives, manuscripts, correspondence, photographs and ephemera and situating them within Carrington's transnational career; Tate notes that a Fellow with knowledge of the Mexican social-political context and of performance histories in the second half of the twentieth century would be well placed. The second, Artist Supported Studios, contributes to research and development for the 2028 Tate Britain Commission through the lens of artists who work with supported studios — organisations that enable disabled and neurodivergent artists to sustain professional practices through long-term studio provision, advocacy and creative support — examining how collaborative artistic practices can be documented and interpreted while remaining attentive to artistic agency. The position is non-salaried, and full time: 36 hours a week for six months, broadly four days at Tate to one at Delfina Foundation. Fellows receive a research resource allowance, travel to Tate Modern, Tate Liverpool and Tate St Ives and to other UK and European institutions, a return economy flight, UK airport transfers, reimbursement of visa fees with support through the visa process, a £40 per day living allowance, a London travel pass, and a single bedroom at the Delfina house, which hosts up to eight residents around shared bathrooms, laundry, kitchen, library and dining room. Fellows get access to Tate's collection, archive, staff and networks, and opportunities to present their own practice at Tate and Delfina events. Open to international researchers based outside the UK. Applications are not made online: the relevant Word application form is downloaded from the Tate listing and emailed to Tate, with an alternative video or audio format available on request. The deadline is Wednesday 21 October 2026 at 17:00 GMT; shortlisted candidates are contacted by 30 October, two rounds of Zoom interviews run between 5 and 27 November, and successful candidates are notified by 4 December 2026. Tate asks that the words in the application be the applicant's own, warning that responses which read as generic or artificially generated could count against an application or see it rejected. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded fellowship + £40/day living allowance.

item.title: Small Wonders · St. Louis Artists' Guild
item.description: A juried exhibition built entirely around scale: every submitted work must measure 11 x 14 inches or smaller, frame included. The Guild frames it as a challenge rather than a restriction — thoughtful composition, experimentation and creative problem-solving inside a compact format, from bold statements to quiet observations. Open to all media and all subject matter, which puts photography on equal footing with painting, printmaking and sculpture, and one of the two jurors is a photographer: Zackary Petot, a multidisciplinary artist working in printmaking, photography and mixed media, and the Guild's Executive & Artistic Director. He judges alongside Kathryn Nahorski, the Guild's former Executive Director and current Development Director, who has spent fourteen years at the organisation and staged hundreds of exhibitions in professional galleries and alternative spaces. The St. Louis Artists' Guild has been running since 1886 and shows in a contemporary gallery and education space at Jackson and Forsyth in Clayton, Missouri. Entrants must be 18 or over and resident in the United States. Work must be original, completed within the last three years, and not previously shown in the Guild's galleries. One application per artist, carrying up to three works; files are JPG or PNG, maximum 1920 pixels on the longest side at 300 dpi, up to 50MB each. Wall-mounted work needs wire and screw eyes, French cleats or another professional hanging device — no saw-tooth hangers, no clip frames — and canvases must be framed or gallery-wrapped. Works must be priced for sale or marked NFS with an insurance value; the Guild insures 65% of the stated value and takes a 35% commission on sales. Accepted work can be hand-delivered or shipped via FedEx or UPS at the artist's cost. The call closes at midnight on October 31, 2026 and the exhibition runs November 20, 2026 to January 2, 2027. The Guild charges an entry fee and prints no amount on either its own call page or the visible prospectus, where EntryThingy shows only "Paid Entry"; the platform's own listing data for this call gives a floor of $10, and the exact charge is settled at checkout after creating an account. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: From $10. Prize: Exhibition.
